ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: The seasonal reversal of winds that governed farming and seaborne trade across the region: sailors timed their voyages to it.
A Greek guide of the mid-1st century CE to the ports and goods from Egypt to East Africa and India, with the earliest historical mention of Aksum.
Grew rich sending African ivory and gold out through its Red Sea port of Adulis, and minted its own gold coins.
From Palembang on Sumatra it ruled the Strait of Malacca from the 7th to the 13th century, taxing the shipping between China and India.
In 1025 a Chola fleet from southern India sacked Srivijaya's ports and seized its ruler, breaking the monopoly it lived on.
An island sultanate that grew rich as the middleman for the gold of the Zimbabwe plateau; Ibn Battuta praised its sultan around 1331.
Seven great fleets under Zheng He reached Arabia and East Africa between 1405 and 1433; then the voyages were ended and never resumed.
Calicut's rulers grew rich on the spice trade with Arab and other Muslim merchants, received Vasco da Gama in 1498 and then fought the Portuguese.
Under its sultanate, founded around 1400, it became South-East Asia's leading entrepôt, until the Portuguese captured it in 1511.
